findings.summary: No run can reach a `reuse` decision: the final tree is compared against a baseline tree captured before the QA-window artifacts the accepted checkpoint commits, so `decideFinalReuse` always returns `evaluate`, and whether an evaluator is dispatched is decided by an undeclared second comparison (`finalTreeId !== acceptedTreeId`). B-02's three reuse stores are therefore unreachable in production and are asserted only by a test that hand-writes the record and hand-emits the event.
findings.evidence:
Probe in this disposable worktree: I added `stageWrites: false` to `finalEvaluationFixture` in src/qa-orchestration.test.ts (production's no-op stage) and printed the decision the orchestrator recorded. `pnpm vitest run src/qa-orchestration.test.ts -t "QA PROBE"` printed:
  PROBE phase: PASS
  PROBE decision: evaluate
  PROBE finalTreeId: ca73af39ebc5d6ea3843adf34caadd09d8d3fb0a
  PROBE baselineTreeId(record): 6e874143d63a38bcf223f1529f0945c5b9732e3e
  PROBE finalCalls: 0
  PROBE reuse events: 0
The two tree IDs differ with nothing written after approval, so the reuse branch is dead. The cause is structural: `writeApprovedBaseline` records `checkpoint.treeId` at src/orchestrator.ts:6272-6276, i.e. the QA checkpoint, while the tree the final decision reads is the accepted checkpoint at src/orchestrator.ts:6574 — which `reviewArtifactViolations` explicitly permits to differ by `qa-report.md` / `qa-review.json` / `stuck.md`. src/orchestrator.ts:6635 then introduces `postApprovalWriteChangedTree = finalTreeId !== acceptedTreeId` and src/orchestrator.ts's `else if (!postApprovalWriteChangedTree)` branch skips final evaluation on that comparison instead of on the reuse decision. The only assertions for B-02 (src/qa-orchestration.test.ts, "records a reuse in run state, run events, and the run summary") call `recordFinalEvaluation(...)` and `logger.event({ type: "final-evaluation-reuse", ... })` directly; they would still pass with the reuse branch deleted from the orchestrator.
findings.expected: contract.md scope lock: "the orchestrator compares the final checkpoint's tree ID against the `approved-baseline.json` record #91 already writes. Equal means reuse: no final evaluator is dispatched, and the reuse is recorded in the slice's own persisted final-evaluation record in `src/run-state.ts`, as a run event in `src/run-events.ts`, and in the slice's `run-summary.md` section." B-02: "A `reuse` decision dispatches zero final-evaluator invocations and records the reuse in three named stores."
findings.observed: A run whose post-approval writing stage writes nothing dispatches zero evaluators (correct) but records `decision: "evaluate"`, journals no `final-evaluation-reuse` event, and renders no `## Final Evaluation Reuse` section — the state the contract describes for that run never occurs. `decideFinalReuse` returns `reuse` for no reachable input, so the reuse marker, its event member, and its logger section are dead code, and the dispatch decision rests on a comparison the contract does not declare.
findings.clearCondition: In a spawned scenario whose post-approval writing stage writes nothing, the orchestrator records `finalEvaluationFor(state, ghIssue)?.decision === "reuse"`, journals exactly one `final-evaluation-reuse` event, renders the slice's `run-summary.md` reuse section, and dispatches zero `evaluator-final` invocations — all read back out of the run the orchestrator performed rather than from a hand-written record or a hand-emitted event; and the tree-changing case still dispatches exactly one evaluator.

findings.summary: P-01's assertion greps source text for `mergeMutex` instead of observing a serialized merge, so it cannot fail if merge serialization broke.
findings.evidence: src/qa-orchestration.test.ts, `it("[behavior:P-01] adds no second lock: the merge mutex in src/wave.ts is untouched")` reads src/wave.ts and asserts `expect(wave).toContain("mergeMutex")`, then asserts three of this slice's own files do not match /mergeMutex|makeAsyncMutex/. Every assertion is a string search over source bytes; none runs a merge. `git diff --name-only 4672247 HEAD` confirms src/wave.ts is unmodified, which is the real evidence for P-01.
findings.expected: acceptance-manifest.json P-01 observableResult: "an it on an existing spawned scenario showing one mutex-serialized merge; no new lock primitive in the diff".
findings.observed: No spawned merge is exercised; the test passes on source text alone and would keep passing if the mutex's critical section were narrowed, so long as the identifier survived.
findings.clearCondition: P-01 is asserted by an executing merge that is observably serialized through the existing `src/wave.ts` mutex, or the assertion is stated as what it actually checks (that this slice adds no lock primitive) with the behavior claim carried by an existing wave-suite assertion cited by id.

findings.summary: No evaluator-final role is ever dispatched: a tree-changing post-approval write terminates the slice with ERROR instead of dispatching one fresh final review.
findings.evidence: src/orchestrator.ts now dispatches `invoke({ role: "evaluator-final", ... })` inside a bounded loop on the post-approval tree, in a disposable worktree from `createReviewIsolation`. `pnpm vitest run src/qa-orchestration.test.ts -t "final evaluation and reuse"` passes `[behavior:B-03] runs an injected post-approval writing stage and evaluates the tree it dirtied exactly once`, which asserts `stageCalls` equals one call at `POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID`, `finalCalls` has length 1, the evaluator's cwd is not the slice worktree and no longer exists after the stage, and `result.phase` is PASS.
findings.expected: One evaluator-final invocation in a disposable worktree after a tree-changing post-approval write, asserted by role and count on a spawned scenario.
findings.observed: Exactly that, asserted on a spawned scenario; the slice reaches PASS rather than ERROR.
findings.clearCondition: A post-approval writing stage that changes the tree causes exactly one evaluator-final invocation in a disposable worktree, and a spawned scenario in src/qa-orchestration.test.ts asserts that one invocation (role and count) after the stub write rather than asserting a slice ERROR.

findings.summary: The wired final verdict can never return PASS: scopeGateStatus is read from gate evidence captured on the pre-write accepted tree and is therefore forced to null in the only branch that evaluates the verdict.
findings.evidence: src/orchestrator.ts now runs `runPostQAGates` with `scopeGateDeclaration` a second time on the final tree (`qaApprovedTreeId: currentFinalTreeId`) and passes `scopeGateStatus: finalScopeEvidence?.treeId === currentFinalTreeId ? statusIn(finalScopeEvidence, SCOPE_GATE_ID) : null`. The spawned scenario `[behavior:B-03] runs an injected post-approval writing stage and evaluates the tree it dirtied exactly once` reaches `result.phase === "PASS"` through `runSliceExecute` with a tree-changing write, which is only reachable when the final verdict returns PASS.
findings.expected: A PASS final verdict reachable through the orchestrator path with a tree-changing post-approval write and a valid final-review.json keyed to the final tree.
findings.observed: PASS reached end to end through `runSliceExecute`, with the scope gate evaluated on the final tree rather than read off the accepted candidate's evidence.
findings.clearCondition: With a tree-changing post-approval write and a valid final-review.json keyed to the final tree, the orchestrator's final verdict returns PASS — because the scope gate is actually evaluated on the final candidate tree — and a test exercises that PASS through the orchestrator path, not only through decideFinalVerdict's arguments.

findings.summary: PersistedFinalEvaluation carries an `attempts` count instead of the per-attempt entries the contract declares, so B-09's observable — every attempt entry keyed to the rejected tree reading as invalidated — cannot be satisfied.
findings.evidence: src/run-state.ts now declares `PersistedFinalEvaluationAttempt` (`attempt`, `candidateTreeId`, `verdict`, `outcome`) and `finalEvaluationFor` returns each entry with `invalidated` derived from `invalidatedCandidateTreeIds`. `[behavior:B-09] appends the rejected tree, drops the baseline citation, and refuses reuse` seeds two attempts on two different trees and asserts the read-back entries equal `[{... invalidated: false}, {... invalidated: true}]`, plus that every entry keyed to the rejected tree is invalidated. The spawned B-09 scenario also asserts `view?.attempts[0]?.invalidated === true` after a real return.
findings.expected: Per-attempt entries keyed to the graded tree, with invalidation readable per entry through `finalEvaluationFor`.
findings.observed: Exactly that, with the invalidation derived on read from the single authority.
findings.clearCondition: `PersistedFinalEvaluation` carries per-attempt entries keyed to the candidate tree each attempt graded, and a test reads back through `finalEvaluationFor` that every entry keyed to an invalidated tree reports as invalidated.

findings.summary: B-09's "generator round counter incremented by exactly one" is asserted as a hard-coded literal on a returned object, and no production code performs the return to the generator loop.
findings.evidence: src/orchestrator.ts routes a `RETURN_TO_GENERATOR` finding by recording a `RETURNED_TO_GENERATOR` attempt entry, calling `invalidateFinalEvaluationBaseline`, setting `generatorFailureSet`/`retryNote` and re-entering the implementation round loop. `[behavior:B-09] returns a baseline-is-wrong finding to the generator loop for exactly one round and no evaluator attempt` reads the counters at each evaluator dispatch and asserts `progress` equals `[{ genRounds: 1, spent: 0 }, { genRounds: 2, spent: 0 }]` — a delta of exactly one generator round with the graded-attempt count unchanged — and that the outcomes read `["RETURNED_TO_GENERATOR", "GRADED"]`.
findings.expected: A real return through the orchestrator, with the generator round counter read before and after and a delta of exactly one, and no final-evaluation attempt spent.
findings.observed: Exactly that, measured from `logger.getSliceProgress` and `finalEvaluationAttemptsSpent` at the dispatches themselves.
findings.clearCondition: A baseline-is-wrong finding drives the orchestrator back into the generator loop, and a test reads the slice's generator round counter before and after that return and asserts a delta of exactly one alongside an unchanged final-evaluation attempt count.

findings.summary: MAX_FINAL_EVALUATION_ATTEMPTS and finalEvaluationAttemptsRemaining have no production call site, so the three-attempt bound refuses nothing.
findings.evidence: src/orchestrator.ts imports both and checks `finalEvaluationAttemptsRemaining({ spent }) === 0` at the top of every loop iteration, before any dispatch. `[behavior:B-10] refuses a fourth final-evaluation attempt against the three-attempt bound` seeds three GRADED attempts, runs `runSliceExecute`, and asserts `result.phase === "ERROR"`, the error text contains `all 3`, and `fixture.finalCalls` has length 0 — the refusal costs no evaluator read.
findings.expected: The dispatch path spends attempts against the bound and refuses the fourth, asserted end to end.
findings.observed: Exactly that; the bound is also credited correctly, since only GRADED entries count and a return to the generator spends none.
findings.clearCondition: The dispatch path spends a final-evaluation attempt against MAX_FINAL_EVALUATION_ATTEMPTS and refuses a fourth, asserted end to end.

findings.summary: final-review.json is parsed twice over the same bytes in the orchestrator's verdict block.
findings.evidence: `validateFinalReview` in src/final-evaluation.ts now returns `{ ok: true; review }`, and src/orchestrator.ts parses once into `reviewValidation` and takes `finalArtifactTreeId` from `reviewValidation.review.finalTreeId`, passing the same value as `reviewValidation` to `decideFinalVerdict`. There is no second read of `finalReviewPath` in the block.
findings.expected: One parse, carried into both the validation result and the finalArtifactTreeId argument.
findings.clearCondition: The verdict block parses final-review.json once and carries the parsed value into both the validation result and the finalArtifactTreeId argument.
